To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Acid-sensing TRCs mediate taste responses of water; 2. Acid-sensing taste cells provide a cue for water detection; 3. Water detection is highly state-dependent.

(1) acid-sensing TRC are required for water detection in taste nerves; (2) acid-sensing taste cells mediate water detection; (3) acid-sensing cells mediate water taste responses in the tongue; and (4) acid-sensing neurons mediate the hedonic value (liking) of water.
acid-sensing TRC cells in taste buds mediate taste responses for water, and these responses are necessary for the detection of external water and the initiation of drinking behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes the sensory information to initiate drinking behavior.
how mammals recognize water and the cellular mechanisms underlying the detection of water in the taste system.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that mediate the perception of taste and the neural circuitry that processes this information to generate the behavioral response of drinking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water is detected by acid-sensitive taste receptors and this detection is dependent on the internal state.
the mammalian taste receptors are able to recognize water as an external cue.
acid-sensing TRC cells are not only responsible for sour detection but also mediate water detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mammalian brain uses the taste system to monitor water in the environment.
acid-sensing TRC is a peripheral detector for water and that the internal state of the animal determines whether this peripheral cue is translated into a hedonic response.
water deprivation induces a state-dependent increase in the hedonic value for water-evoked responses, and this increase is mediated by acid-sensing TRC neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acid-sensing TRC is not a sour taste sensor but rather a water sensor that is activated by both acid and water.
acid-sensing TRC neurons are the peripheral detectors for water.
water detection in mammals is not a passive process but rather requires the activation of a specialized taste system.
